lead: Lincoln plumbing deals with deep cold, hard water, basements and older brick neighborhoods. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Lincoln.
risk: frozen pipes, hard water scale and aging pipes in older homes
risk_short: frozen pipes, hard water and old pipes
why: The Near South, Everett and University Place have homes from the 1890s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and clay sewer laterals. Nearly every home has a basement.
Winters freeze pipes near exterior walls and in unheated spaces. Spring rain tests sump pumps and basement drains.
water: Lincoln pumps its water from wells along the Platte River near Ashland and pipes it to the city. It is hard, so scale builds up in heaters and fixtures.
tips: Keep the heat on and cabinets open in deep cold.
Test your sump pump each spring.
Scope the sewer line before buying an older home.
areas: PipeMend works in the Near South, Everett, College View, Bethany, Havelock, University Place, the Haymarket and every other Lincoln neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits and local plumber licenses come from the City of Lincoln Building and Safety Department. Nebraska has no statewide plumber license.

faq.a: Nebraska has no statewide plumber license, so Lincoln licenses plumbers through its Building and Safety Department. Ask for the city license number before work starts.
